title: Proper exchange for a simplicial etale augmentation
statement:
Let $a:U_\bullet\to X$ be an augmented simplicial scheme [def-pc-scheme] such that every component augmentation $a_p:U_p\to X$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $g:Y\to X$ be any scheme morphism, let $V_\bullet=U_\bullet\times_XY$ [def-pc-fibre-product], let $a':V_\bullet\to Y$ be the augmentation and $g_\bullet:V_\bullet\to U_\bullet$ the projection. The total etale topoi have sheaves described by component sheaves and compatible inverse-image transition maps, as in [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-image-spectral-sequence]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring annihilated by an integer $m\ge1$, and let $L\in D^+(U_\bullet,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The ordinary adjunction-mate exchange map is an isomorphism
$$g^*Ra_*L\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra'_*g_\bullet^*L.$$
It is natural in $L$, respects the canonical derived composition identifications for maps of augmented simplicial schemes, and uses the units and counits of the ordinary inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions. No Cartesianity condition on the transition maps of $L$, constructibility, finite-type hypothesis on $Y$, or upper cohomological bound on $L$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D7F (lemma-augmentation-spectral-sequence-modules) and Tag 0D99 (lemma-morphism-augmentation-simplicial-sites), applied to the degreewise proper exchange of etale-cohomology.tex Tag 095T (theorem-proper-base-change); the simplicial use is also explicit in Orgogozo Lemma 3.1.1, p. 6, both displayed isomorphisms.

proof.text: For constant $\Lambda$ coefficients, $g^*$ and every $g_p^*$ are the exact module inverse images of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The component description in [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-image-spectral-sequence] gives $(g_\bullet^*F)_p=g_p^*F_p$, with transitions obtained by pulling back those of $F$. Kernels and cokernels of families are computed componentwise: the transition inverse images are exact, so the component kernels and cokernels inherit the transition maps and satisfy the corresponding universal properties. Consequently $g_\bullet^*$ is exact as well. Componentwise commutativity $a'_p{}^*g^*\cong g_p^*a_p^*$ gives $\theta:a'^*g^*\cong g_\bullet^*a^*$ on families. Define $\beta_L$ to be its derived mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]: its transpose is $g_\bullet^*\varepsilon_{a,L}\circ\theta_{Ra_*L}$. This fixes the ordinary units and counits before proving invertibility.

Fix $c\in\mathbf Z$ with $H^q(L)=0$ for $q<c$. Work with small site models in a sufficiently large fixed universe: the total site has the set of pairs $(p,W)$ with $p\in\mathbf N$ and $W$ in the chosen component site. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] its module category is Grothendieck and every complex has a quasi-isomorphism to a termwise-injective K-injective complex. Applying this to $F[0]$, the degree-zero map $F\to I^0$ is monic, because its composite to $H^0(I)$ is an isomorphism; thus the category has enough injectives. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] to choose bounded-below injective complexes $I$ representing $L$ and $J$ representing $g_\bullet^*L$, both zero below $c$; these complexes are K-injective. Exactness from step 1 identifies $Q(g_\bullet^*I)$ with $g_\bullet^*L$. The isomorphism $Q(g_\bullet^*I)\cong QJ$ is represented by a chain map $j:g_\bullet^*I\to J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. This map is a quasi-isomorphism because its image under localization is the chosen isomorphism. Component restriction is exact by [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-image-spectral-sequence], so $I_p$ represents $L_p$, and $J_p$ represents $g_p^*L_p$.

Form the two double complexes $A^{p,q}=g^*a_{p,*}I_p^q$ and $B^{p,q}=a'_{p,*}J_p^q$, for $p\ge0$ and $q\ge c$, with alternating-face horizontal differential and total differential $d_{\rm face}+(-1)^p d_{\rm resolution}$. The double-complex computation asserted in [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-image-spectral-sequence] gives augmentation quasi-isomorphisms $a_*I\to\operatorname{Tot}(a_{p,*}I_p^q)$ and $a'_*J\to\operatorname{Tot}(B)$. Exactness of $g^*$ preserves the first quasi-isomorphism and the finite sums in every total degree; preservation of cohomology follows from [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology]. Thus $g^*a_*I\to\operatorname{Tot}(A)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and the total complexes represent $g^*Ra_*L$ and $Ra'_*g_\bullet^*L$. The column spectral sequences have $E_1^{p,q}=g^*H^q(Ra_{p,*}L_p)$ and ${E'}_1^{p,q}=H^q(Ra'_{p,*}g_p^*L_p)$.

Let $e_p:g^*a_{p,*}\to a'_{p,*}g_p^*$ be the underived mate of the component square. Define $t^{p,q}=a'_{p,*}(j_p^q)\circ e_{p,I_p^q}:A^{p,q}\to B^{p,q}$. Naturality of a mate makes these maps commute with the resolution differential. For a face $u:U_{p+1}\to U_p$ and its pullback $v:V_{p+1}\to V_p$, the horizontal map is adjoint to the transition $u^*I_p^q\to I_{p+1}^q$, using $a_{p+1}=a_pu$. Apply part 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to the squares for $u$ and $a_p$: the mate for $a_{p+1}$ is their pasted mate. Naturality in that transition, followed by the equality expressing that $j$ respects transitions, says exactly $t^{p+1,q}d_i^A=d_i^B t^{p,q}$ for each face $i$. Taking alternating sums proves horizontal commutativity. Hence $t:A\to B$ is a double-complex map, preserving the filtration by $p$; the sign $(-1)^p$ is the same on both sides.

proof.text: The augmented column $p=-1$ of this comparison is $e=a'_*(j)\circ e_a:g^*a_*I\to a'_*J$, where $e_a$ is the underived augmentation mate. The same pasting calculation as in step 4 makes the augmentation quasi-isomorphisms of step 3 intertwine $e$ and $\operatorname{Tot}(t)$. To identify $Q(e)$, transpose under $a'^*\dashv Ra'_*$: on these resolutions the transpose is the class of $a'^*g^*a_*I\xrightarrow{\theta}g_\bullet^*a^*a_*I\xrightarrow{g_\bullet^*\varepsilon_a}g_\bullet^*I\xrightarrow{j}J$. The first two arrows transpose to $e_a$ by the defining hom bijection of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; postcomposition with $j$ transposes to $a'_*(j)\circ e_a$ by its naturality. Since $I,J$ are K-injective and $Q(j)$ is the chosen resolution identification, this is precisely the derived counit transpose in step 1, under the adjunction-normalized derived identifications of [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-image-spectral-sequence]. Bijectivity of the hom adjunction gives $Q(e)=\beta_L$. Thus $t$ compares the actual exchange map on abutments.

source.place: Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change); spaces-simplicial.tex Tag 0D7F and its augmentation comparison

proof.text: Under the canonical column comparisons in [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-image-spectral-sequence], transpose the map induced by $t$ in column $p$ under $a'_p{}^*\dashv Ra'_{p,*}$. As in step 5, the defining mate identity followed by $j_p$ gives $a'_p{}^*g^*Ra_{p,*}L_p\xrightarrow{\theta_p}g_p^*a_p^*Ra_{p,*}L_p\xrightarrow{g_p^*\varepsilon_{a_p}}g_p^*L_p$. Thus the column map is the ordinary component exchange; this uses the canonical column-derived-image comparisons, not any assertion that $I_p$ or $J_p$ is K-injective. Now $L_p$ is bounded below, $a_p$ is proper, and $V_p=U_p\times_XY$. Also $m\Lambda=0$ implies $mH^q(L_p)=0$, so underlying cohomology is torsion. Apply [det-properbasechange-modules], which allows an arbitrary commutative ring, arbitrary base change and torsion underlying cohomology. The component exchange is an isomorphism. Exact pullback preserves cohomology by [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology], so $t$ is an isomorphism on every $E_1^{p,q}$.

source.place: Tags 095T (theorem-proper-base-change) and 0DDE (lemma-proper-base-change), with constant-module coefficient comparison det-properbasechange-modules

proof.text: Reindex by $q\mapsto q-c$: then $A$ and $B$ are first-quadrant double complexes with the same total differential $d_{\rm face}+(-1)^pd_{\rm resolution}$ and total complexes shifted by $c$. By [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] their first spectral sequences have $E_1$ the column cohomology, abut to the column filtration of $\operatorname{Tot}$ with $E_\infty\cong\operatorname{gr}$, and are functorial for morphisms of double complexes; so $t$ induces a morphism of spectral sequences compatible with the abutment filtrations and these identifications, and on $E_1$ it is the column map of step 6. An isomorphism on $E_1$ induces an isomorphism on $E_2$, since $E_2$ is the homology of $E_1$. Apply [lem-sp-page-induction] to conclude that the comparison is an isomorphism on every subsequent page and on $E_\infty$. Stabilization is harmless here: both spectral sequences vanish outside $p\ge0$, $q\ge c$, and the differentials have bidegree $(r,1-r)$. At a fixed $(p,q)$, incoming differentials have zero source when $r>p$ and outgoing differentials have zero target when $r>q-c+1$. Thus the $E_\infty$ objects and their comparison are the eventually constant pages at each bidegree, exactly the abutment graded pieces supplied by [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-image-spectral-sequence].

Fix $n$ and put $N=\max(n-c+1,0)$. The source filtration is $g^*F^pH^n(Ra_*L)$ and the target is $F^pH^n(Ra'_*g_\bullet^*L)$; the first is indeed a filtration of $H^n(g^*Ra_*L)$ because exact $g^*$ preserves cohomology, subobjects and quotients by [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology]. Both filtrations have $F^0=H^n$ and $F^N=0$ by [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-image-spectral-sequence]. The filtered map $t$ induces $H^n(\beta_L)$ by step 5, and its graded maps are the $E_\infty^{p,n-p}$ isomorphisms of step 7, by the functoriality of the identification $E_\infty\cong\operatorname{gr}$ in [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences]. Apply [lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction] to obtain that $H^n(\beta_L)$ is an isomorphism. When $n<c$, $N=0$ and both abutments are zero. The bound $N$ depends on $n$, so no uniform cohomological dimension bound is required.

The preceding argument holds for every integer $n$. Both sides are bounded below by $c$, as is also visible from their augmentation double complexes. The cohomology criterion [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] therefore proves that $\beta_L:g^*Ra_*L\to Ra'_*g_\bullet^*L$ is an isomorphism in $D^+(Y,\Lambda)$.

source.place: Derived categories: localization at quasi-isomorphisms, as stated in lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology

proof.text: Naturality in $L$ holds because $\beta$ was defined as a natural-transformation mate, rather than by choosing the inverse produced by the spectral sequence. For composition, let $h:W_\bullet\to U_\bullet$ be a map over $X$, put $b=ah$, and let $h':W'_\bullet\to V_\bullet$ and $k_\bullet:W'_\bullet\to W_\bullet$ be its base changes. Write $\beta_h:g_\bullet^*Rh_*\to Rh'_*k_\bullet^*$ for its ordinary exchange, without assuming it invertible. Under the canonical composition comparisons, part 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] gives the explicit identity $\beta_b=(Ra'_*\beta_h)\circ(\beta_a Rh_*)$. Part 1 gives the analogous identity for successive changes of $X$. The derived composition comparisons in [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-image-spectral-sequence] are normalized by the composite inverse-image adjunction, so these identities concern exactly the specified composition maps. For identity squares the mate is the identity by part 4. In particular no adjunction unit or counit is rescaled or replaced; all compatibilities are with the ordinary adjunctions used in step 1.

I also read the sources: Stacks 0D7F statement and proof, 0D99, 095T and 0DDE, with all tags checked against tags/tags. No SGA source is used. The statement adds no hypothesis and drops none. On the components, the exchange is the counit-defined mate, the same as Ex^Λ of det-properbasechange-modules. Each component square V_p=U_p×_X Y is Cartesian, and torsion follows from mΛ=0. Edge cases checked: g=id, L=0, Λ=0, constant augmentation, shifts. Duplicate search found nothing; lem-trf-nearby-proper-source-exchange states something different. Steps 1-6 and 9-10 are correct: the enough-injectives argument holds, j is represented through K-injective Hom, the face-wise mate pasting is right, Q(e)=β_L follows by transposition, and the column exchange uses no K-injectivity of I_p or J_p. In step 7 the stabilization bounds r>p and r>q-c+1 are right, and in step 8 N=max(n-c+1,0) is right. One fault (C1/C4): steps 7 and 8 used, without citation, that the double-complex map t between A on Y and B induces a morphism of spectral sequences compatible with E_∞≅gr. The simplicial node is functorial only in L. Fixed: after reindexing q↦q-c, both steps now cite thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences, which has the same sign convention d_I+(-1)^p d_II, is functorial for morphisms of double complexes, and is Lean-closed in slopmaster2. proof_deps is recomputed and a tool_uses entry is added.
